label: personal_4:fb-text
text: Funny thing about AI phone agents: the ones that look perfect in a chat window often fall over on the first real call. People ring stressed, talk over each other, answer questions you haven't even asked yet. The trick is writing for that chaos, not for a tidy conversation that never happens. Have you ever rung a business and got trapped by a robot that clearly expected you to behave? 😅

label: personal_4:li-text
text:
I watched a voice agent fall apart on its first real call recently. Clean as anything in ChatGPT. Then a bloke rang at 7am, boiler dead, talking over the top of it, giving his postcode, his problem and his availability all in one breath.

The prompt assumed a polite caller who waits their turn. Real callers don't.

Here's what actually holds up.

Give the agent a tight system role, not a vague description. For a plumber: you take job details and availability, you do NOT quote prices, you escalate genuine emergencies straight away.

Cap responses to roughly ten seconds of speech. Three paragraphs and the caller is gone before sentence two.

Assume people interrupt, mumble, and answer questions you haven't asked yet. Build for the mess, not the ideal.

The tech is rarely the problem. The prompt written by someone who has never listened to a real call usually is.

text:
Google just launched Gemini Spark, an AI agent that works on its own across your files and messages. It's genuinely impressive in a demo.

I still wouldn't hand it a law firm's intake phone. Not yet.

Here's the mismatch. Autonomous agents are built for async work. You give it a task, it goes away for hours, it reports back. Fine for research. Useless when someone's calling right now about a car accident and won't wait more than a ring or two before phoning the next firm on the list.

Then there's access. An always-on agent needs to read your emails, calendar and documents to be useful. Intake calls involve criminal charges, immigration status, medical details. That sensitive stuff getting processed on servers you don't control, under a privacy policy you never signed? That's a compliance problem waiting to happen.

And the demo-to-reality gap is real. These agents shine on clean inputs. Callers are messy and emotional.

Right tool, wrong job. Use the narrow thing that answers in real time and keeps the data where it belongs.
